named_subject: A rhinoceros, drawn as two overlapping ovals (body and head) with zigzag horns and stick legs.
evidence: Placement matches the film: the leftward shift in frames 9-12 and the slight return in 13-16 track the rhino's position in d.png frames 9-16. But the head never moves the way the film's head does: in film frames 1-4 the head is pressed down with the horn in the dirt and in 9-16 it bobs while rooting, whereas in the animation the head outline is the same from frame 1 to 16 and only the horn zigzag changes. The jaw stroke present in frames 1-3 disappears at frame 4 (pop). The horn zigzag is redrawn with different spike lengths and counts in frames 8, 11, 12 and 16 (long spike reaching the frame edge in 8, 11, 12, short again in 13). The front leg pair jumps position under the belly between frames 3-4, 8-9 and 12-13. The tail swings that are visible in every film frame are absent.
primary_gap: The head does not perform the film's rooting action: it stays fixed while the horns are redrawn at changing lengths, so the only visible change is spikes flickering rather than a head dipping and bobbing at the ground.
closes_when: Across frames 1-16 the whole head shape (oval, front edge and horns together, at constant horn size) tilts and dips so the horn tip touches the ground line in frames 1-4 and bobs down-up in frames 9-16, with the horn zigzag keeping the same shape in every frame.
protect: The doodle's construction (two overlapping open ovals, straight front edge, zigzag horn triangles, paired stick legs, wobbly hand-drawn polyline strokes); the grey fence and post scenery placed as in the film; the leftward drift in frames 9-12 that matches the film's framing.
identity_gap: The drawing is the doodle mirrored to face right with its stroke habits kept, but the head oval has grown to nearly the size of the body, whereas in c.png the head is clearly smaller than the body.
